sources.entry: Swamp Converter - Menu bar file converter: drag a file, tap a key and drop it on a wheel to convert video, audio, images and PDFs. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/aansonsa/swamp-converter) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu-bar app that opens a radial "wheel" over a dragged file so you can convert, compress or tidy it, and download videos from YouTube and other yt-dlp-supported sites.
summary.what_it_does: Swamp Converter is a macOS app that opens a radial menu under the pointer when you drag a file and tap Shift, Control, Option, or shake the file. Dropping the file on a sector starts an operation such as converting to PNG, compressing, or making a PDF. Holding Command on release opens the operation in the Studio, a larger window with full options, a preview and a queue. The README lists image, video, audio, PDF and document, subtitle and archive operations, plus "fit to size" presets for messaging apps and social posts. A shortcut (⌃⌥Space) works on a browser page, a Finder selection or a clipboard image, and ⌃⌥D downloads the current page. Downloads use yt-dlp, which is not bundled and can be installed from the Settings window after consent; the wheel offers quality choices up to 8K. The app also has Finder Services, a Floating Shelf, watched folders, and a "swamp" command line. The README says there is no telemetry or account, and the app is about 10 MB.
use_cases: convert photos between HEIC, JPG, PNG and WebP on a Mac
compress a video or PDF before sending it
shrink a file to fit a WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord or email size limit
download a YouTube video in high quality or as audio
merge, split or OCR PDF files
batch-convert files from a watched folder
trim, mute or speed up a video clip
how_to_run: Download SwampConverter.zip from the latest release and unzip it.
Open it; if macOS blocks it, approve it under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
Optional: run ./build.sh package to build from source with Command Line Tools.
Optional: run scripts/install.sh to install into ~/Applications and link the swamp command.
notable: Radial 'wheel' menu that opens under the pointer while dragging a file, with Shift, Control, Option or shake triggers
Studio window for full options, before/after preview and a job queue, opened by holding Command on release
Download video up to 8K via yt-dlp with a 'Maximum quality' option and audio-only modes
Ships a swamp command line, Finder Services, watched folders and a Floating Shelf
Conversions are checked on real files by an independent content check, per the README's conversion matrix
caveats: Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or newer on Apple silicon, and the app is English only.
Ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS asks for manual approval on first launch and may ask for permissions again after updates.
yt-dlp and a JavaScript runtime are needed for downloads; DRM-protected video is not supported, and the README warns that site terms may restrict downloading.
Several operations need optional tools (ffmpeg, LibreOffice, Pandoc, ImageMagick, cwebp) that are not bundled; those options show dimmed until installed.
